archetype.name: Pocket Passer (intermediate-first)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who hardly runs anymore and earns his value attacking the middle of the field and beyond 10 air yards from shotgun, while the quick game and his pocket escapes drag him down.

report.headline: Pushing the ball downfield works; the pocket and third downs still fail him
report.take:
Bryce Young's fourth season is the best of his career, though the gain is modest and the yardage overstates it. His 2023 rookie year was a 5.46-yards-per-attempt struggle. 2024 and 2025 settled into roughly average efficiency (0.006 and 0.010 EPA a play). This year he sits at 0.041 EPA per dropback, 21st of 55, with 7.2 yards an attempt, up 0.9 on last season. The 265 passing yards a game (7th) are a different matter: they come partly from context. Carolina passes more than the situation calls for (6th in pass rate over expected), and its defense ranks 31st in sack rate and last in hit rate. That defense lets games turn into shootouts that keep him throwing, which is why he's 76.9 yards a game ahead of last year on a far smaller efficiency gain.

The engine is clear in the depth splits. His throws of 10+ air yards have added 62.3 EPA, while everything under 10 sits slightly below zero. Throws behind the line alone have cost 13.4 points, with completion over expected at -9.3. Over the middle he has been outstanding: 74.2% completions, 12.1 points over expected, 45.1 EPA, no interceptions. Deep balls return 0.701 EPA a throw on 41 attempts, a strong but small sample that will cool. He isn't a reckless gunslinger. His aggressiveness ticked up only slightly from last season and his bad-throw rate dropped. He's a timing passer who is better when the route breaks inside at depth than when the play is designed to be easy.

The averages hide the drag points. His pressure-to-sack rate (26.1%, 15th of 45) is worse than the low-20s marks he posted in 2024 and 2025, and he barely scrambles now: 8 all season, down to 4.6 rushing yards a game from 13.5. On third down that adds up. He faces 8 yards to go on average, has been sacked 15 times in 98 plays, converts 32.7% and has lost 24.9 points of EPA, wiping out most of what he builds on early downs. In one-score games he's slightly below average (-0.021), and in close fourth quarters worse (-0.102). Some of the efficiency comes while trailing by 9+ (0.097), and the red zone has yielded 13 touchdowns on sub-50% completions and negative EPA.

The path matters. Weeks 1-4 were excellent (+12.5, +10.4, +15.7 EPA in three of them). Then Tampa Bay and Green Bay sank him: -16.0 and -6.4 with 11 sacks combined. The last five games are underwater at -0.106 EPA per dropback with a 10.7% sack rate. The last three show accuracy coming back (67.7% completions, +2.9 CPOE) but EPA per dropback still only 0.024. He has looked better lately, but the early-season peak hasn't returned.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep accuracy
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards carry his whole season: 62.3 EPA added and 6.4 points of completion over expected, against a slightly negative short game. That fits his career arc: a passer whose accuracy and anticipation at depth improved steadily since 2023. The intermediate part (78 attempts, 0.431 EPA) looks durable. The deep number (0.701 on 41 attempts) is real skill inflated by a small sample and should drift down.

strengths.title: Owning the middle of the field
strengths.body: Between the hashes he completes 74.2% at 12.1 points over expected with zero interceptions, by far his best direction. Outside throws, especially to the left, are roughly break-even. It suggests he reads leverage well and trusts in-breakers to Waller and McMillan, whose 0.371 and 0.232 EPA per target lead his main receivers. Some of that clean interception line is luck, but the success rate (61.8%) says the accuracy is real.

strengths.title: Volume baked into the environment
strengths.body: Carolina passes 2.7 points above expectation (6th), and a defense near the bottom in sack and hit rate keeps scoreboards busy. That is why his yardage ranks 7th while his efficiency ranks 21st. As long as the defense can't get home, the volume holds.

concerns.title: Third downs end in sacks
concerns.body: On third down he's sacked 15 times in 98 plays and converts under a third. The phase has cost 24.9 EPA, more than his whole season's passing EPA. Long yardage (8 to go on average) is partly the offense's fault, but holding the ball without scrambling is his. This is the single biggest thing between him and a top-12 efficiency season.

concerns.title: Pocket escape has regressed
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate (26.1%) is worse than his 2024-25 levels. His 8% sack rate ranks 34th, and over the last five games it rose to 10.7%. He's not extending plays with his legs anymore, so sacks aren't being bought back with scrambles. Several heavy-sack games, like 5 against Tampa Bay at only 18.2% pressure, point to coverage sacks, which are on the quarterback.

concerns.title: Quick game is dead weight
concerns.body: Screens and throws behind the line have cost 13.4 EPA at 9.3 points under expected completion, and under-10 throws as a group are slightly negative. Part of this is scheme and blocking on screens, not him. Still, the offense lacks an easy-yards release valve, which makes third-and-long more common.

trend.note: He was hot through Week 4, then crashed against Tampa Bay and Green Bay, and the last five games are negative at -0.106 EPA per dropback. The last three show accuracy recovering (+2.9 CPOE) but efficiency and volume still below his season marks.

nextGame.headline: Rematch with the defense that buried him in Week 7
nextGame.body:
Tampa Bay ranks 3rd in defensive EPA and 2nd against the pass. It is 4th in short-throw EPA allowed, which is the area he already struggles in, and it erased him in Week 7: 163 yards, two interceptions, five sacks, -16.0 EPA. He threw short that day (6.8 intended air yards) and got nothing. The opening is deep: Tampa ranks 24th in deep EPA allowed and generates few hits or sacks (28th in sack rate). It barely blitzed him last time. If Carolina lets him push the ball to the intermediate and deep middle, his best zone meets their weakest. The Book has Carolina as a 3-point road underdog with a 43.5 total. Tampa's run-heavy, inefficient offense points to a lower-volume game than his shootouts.

Availability tilts somewhat his way. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (89% of snaps) is out, which removes the player most responsible for policing the middle and deep thirds. Corners Jacob Parrish (81%) and Benjamin Morrison are questionable after MRIs, and Josh Hayes is on IR, so the secondary could be thin. On Carolina's side, guard Brady Christensen hasn't played this season and backup back Jonathon Brooks is out. Neither changes his protection or targets much.

keyMatchups.title: Deep middle without Winfield
keyMatchups.body: His deep throws return 0.701 EPA, and Tampa allows 0.573 EPA on deep balls, 24th in the league. With their starting safety out, the seams and deep crossers should be more open than in Week 7. Whether Canales calls them is the question.

keyMatchups.title: McMillan against a WR1 lockdown
keyMatchups.body: Tampa has held opposing WR1s furthest below their averages of any defense, at -0.32 EPA per target. McMillan is his most-targeted receiver, so Young will need Waller and the WR2 spot, where Tampa ranks 29th, to carry more. Coker's 0.032 EPA per target makes that a shaky fallback.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into a strength
keyMatchups.body: Tampa is 4th in short-pass EPA allowed, and his throws under 10 yards are already slightly negative. A dink-and-dunk plan repeats Week 7.

nextGame.watch: His intended air yards and sack count. If he's throwing past the sticks and keeping sacks to two or three against a light pass rush, he can win this; if he's checking down and taking coverage sacks again, it's Week 7 all over.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is mostly sustainable. Carolina's pass-leaning approach and a defense that can't pressure will keep him near 35 attempts, though the 4,507-yard pace from the hot start is too high. Expect something like 225-265 yards a game, closer to his last-three level than his season mark. His intermediate and middle-of-field accuracy has built up over three seasons and should hold. The deep efficiency and the clean interception line between the hashes will cool.

What decides whether this is a real step forward is the pocket. Sacks on third down are erasing his early-down work, and his rushing has nearly vanished, so nothing offsets them. If the sack rate drifts back toward his 2024-25 form, his efficiency settles in the top 15. If it stays near the last five games' level, he's a high-volume, roughly average passer whose fantasy line outpaces his real value. Red-zone touchdowns on sub-50% completions are a mild regression risk.
swingFactors: How often the offense calls 10+ air-yard throws vs screens

confidence.note: Ten starts in a stable role, but game-to-game swings are large and the deep split is a small sample.
